newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel little changed in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel little changed in quiet trading.

text.p: The shekel representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar on Thursday in thin trading after Wednesday's interest rate cut and a cabinet vote to widen the Israeli currency's trading band, dealers said.
"The market is extremely quiet today as investors need some time to digest the recent changes," said Zahi Elias at Bank Leumi.
"The market is responding as if the interest rate cut did not have a very dramatic impact," a trader at Bank Hapoalim added.

After the government approved foreign exchange reforms on Wednesday, triggering the resignation of Finance Minister Dan Meridor, the Bank of Israel lowered its key lending rate by 1.2 percentage points to an annual 12.7 percent.
"The shekel is stable and sitting close to its lower limit and hasn't moved much from its closing price yesterday," said a dealer at First International Bank of Israel.
"Investors remained on the sidelines and trading was trendless. It's difficult to predict where the market is going," Elias said.

The central bank hopes that with the foreign exchange changes it will not need to intervene as much in the currency market. But some traders said the Bank of Israel might still have to buy dollars to keep the shekel from strengthening beyond its bounds.
"The shekel is still barely above its lower limit. In the near future the bank will need to intervene again," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4190 shekels against 3.4200 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7133 against 3.7155 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0182 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0091 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9753 shekels compared with 1.9802 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4200 shekels.
-- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
